styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old Batavia, museums and the city's many faces.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Street warungs, night markets and regional dishes.

styles.label: Shopping
styles.blurb: Big malls, batik and craft markets.

stays.why: Central for the MRT, big malls and the National Monument; easy to reach most sights.
Cafés, restaurants and nightlife; quieter streets than the centre.
Next to Old Batavia (Kota Tua) and its museums; good for history-focused days.
Waterfront parks and family attractions; cooler breeze but far from the centre.

food: Try Jakarta staples: nasi goreng, sate ayam, gado-gado and kerak telor, an egg-and-rice street snack.
Eat at night markets and street warungs for cheap, fresh food; look for busy stalls with local queues.
Padang restaurants serve ready-made spicy dishes piled high; you pay for what you eat.
In malls, food courts are clean and cheap; sit-down restaurants cost more but are reliable.
Tap water is not safe to drink. Drink bottled or filtered water, and be careful with ice from street stalls.
more_time: Add a day trip to Bogor for the botanical gardens and cooler hills; check train times on the day.
History fans can spend a half day in Kota Tua: the old town square, museum and harbour area.
Families can swap a mall day for Ancol's waterfront parks and attractions.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Old Batavia, a museum and a food crawl; add a night if you want a Bogor day trip.

month_notes: Jan: very wet, about 28 rain days. Carry an umbrella and plan indoor sights.
Feb: still very wet, about 27 rain days. Short heavy afternoon showers are common.
Mar: one of the wettest months, about 29 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
Apr: wet, about 28 rain days. Mornings are often the driest window.
May: rain eases to about 22 days. Good balance of heat and showers.
Jun: drier, about 20 rain days. A comfortable month for walking tours.
Jul: one of the driest months, about 12 rain days. Hot but good for sightseeing.
Aug: dry and hot, about 11 rain days. The best month for outdoor plans.
Sep: driest feel, about 14 rain days, highs near 33°C. Start early to beat the heat.
Oct: rain returns, about 21 days. Pack a light rain jacket.
Nov: wet again, about 26 rain days. Expect afternoon downpours.
Dec: wet, about 26 rain days. Busy holiday season, so book hotels early.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, around 30–33°C by day and 23–24°C at night. Rain is common, heaviest from November to April.

items.title: Wet season: November to April
items.text: Expect 26–29 rain days a month. Showers are often heavy but short; carry an umbrella.

items.title: Driest months: July to September
items.text: About 11–14 rain days. Best window for outdoor sights, though it stays hot.

items.title: Hot and humid all year
items.text: Highs of 30–33°C with high humidity. Plan outdoor time for early morning.

items.title: Pack for rain
items.text: A compact umbrella or rain jacket and quick-dry shoes help in the wet months.

items.title: Stay hydrated
items.text: Drink bottled water often; tap water is not safe to drink.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, sunscreen and a light layer for air-conditioned malls and trains.

transit.best: Use the MRT and TransJakarta for main routes; Grab or Gojek for the rest.

modes.text: Jakarta MRT runs Lebak Bulus to Bundaran HI, every 5–10 min, 05:00–midnight.
TransJakarta BRT has 14 mainlines on dedicated lanes; fares Rp2,000–20,000 with one card.
KAI Commuter trains link suburbs and run 04:30–midnight; Jabodebek and Jakarta LRT cover more areas.
Grab and Gojek are the main ride apps; metered taxis exist but agree on price or use the meter.
Driving is slow and congested; odd-even plate rules apply on some toll roads on weekdays.
Walking long distances is impractical; use apps or transit between areas.
